title: A full stack: web, api, postgres, redis
summary: Read and run a realistic compose file, and work with it day to day.

steps.title: The whole stack
body: A Next.js front end, a .NET API, Postgres and Redis. Only the web front end is published to the host; everything else is reachable only inside the project network.
`DB_PASSWORD` comes from `.env`. The API reaches `db` and `redis` by service name; the browser reaches only `localhost:3000`.

steps.prompt: Why does the file above publish no ports for `db` and `redis`?
options: Only the web front end needs to be reached from outside; the API talks to them over the project network
Postgres and Redis cannot be published
Ports are only allowed on `build:` services
steps.explain: Fewer published ports, less attack surface. For local debugging you can add `ports: ["5433:5432"]` in a `compose.override.yaml`, which Compose merges automatically.

steps.prompt: Match each symptom in this stack to its cause.
pairs: web's server-side code logs `fetch failed` calling `http://localhost:8080`
inside the web container, localhost is web itself: call `http://api:8080` (the `API_URL` above)
api logs `password authentication failed` after changing DB_PASSWORD
the pgdata volume was initialised with the old password
api starts before Postgres is ready
the code change does not show up after `docker compose up -d`
the image was not rebuilt: add `--build`

steps.prompt: You run `docker compose logs api`. Compose prefixes each line with the container name. Write the first line, if the API's first output is `Now listening on: http://[::]:8080`, the project is `shop`, and Compose aligns with a single space after the bar.
steps.explain: Lines from each container are prefixed with its name and a `|`. Add `--no-log-prefix` to drop the prefix.

steps.prompt: Arrange a typical day: start the stack, follow the API, change its code, apply the change, and finally tear down **including** the database.
steps.explain: `up -d --build api` rebuilds just that image and recreates its container; the rest keeps running.

steps.prompt: You changed only the API's environment in compose.yaml. What is the quickest correct way to apply it?
options: `docker compose up -d` (Compose sees the changed config and recreates only the api container)
steps.explain: `restart` reuses the existing container with its **old** configuration. `up` compares and recreates what changed.

steps.prompt: Point the API at the other services by name.

steps.title: Fix a full stack
prompt: This terminal has a **real Docker Engine** with Compose. `~/shop/compose.yaml` is a web, API and database stack
written in a hurry. It has **three** bugs. Bring it up, read what happens, and fix them:
cd ~/shop && docker compose up -d --wait; docker compose ps -a; docker compose logs
When it is right: `docker compose up -d --wait` succeeds, `curl http://localhost:8080/` prints `web 1.0`, the API
connected to the database, and the database's data (it says where it keeps it) survives `docker compose down` and

checks.name: web answers on localhost:8080
checks.fail: `curl http://localhost:8080/` does not print `web 1.0`. Ports are `"HOST:CONTAINER"`.

checks.name: the API is running and connected
checks.cmd: cd ~/shop && docker compose logs --no-log-prefix api | tail -n 1
checks.fail: The API is not connected. Its log says which host it tries: inside a container `localhost` is itself.

checks.name: the database's data directory is on the volume
checks.cmd: cd ~/shop && docker compose config --format json | jq -r '.services.db.volumes[] | select(.type=="volume") | "\(.source) \(.target)"'
checks.fail: The `dbdata` volume is not mounted where the database keeps its data (`docker compose logs db` says where).

checks.name: all three are up
checks.fail: Not all services are up after `docker compose up -d --wait`.

hints: `docker compose ps -a` and `docker compose logs api` show which service fails and why.
Three bugs: a reversed port mapping, `DB_HOST: localhost`, and a volume mounted on a folder the database does not use.
solution: sed -i 's/"80:8080"/"8080:80"/; s/DB_HOST: localhost/DB_HOST: db/; s#dbdata:/data#dbdata:/var/lib/db#' compose.yaml
steps.explain: Each bug is a classic: `HOST:CONTAINER` written backwards, `localhost` meaning the container itself, and a volume on a path the app never writes, which silently loses data on the next `down`. `docker compose logs` named all three; `up --wait` turned "looks started" into "is healthy".
